pressure_yard.name: Pressure Yard
pressure_yard.description: A 5.40 m rack standing all four scenes of the `selection` family side by side, each population drawn as six order statistics on one shared 3.20 m travel under one datum rail. SIX registry names resolve to FOUR scenes, so four bays is the whole family and nothing has been dropped. The four agree on the vocabulary - drift, uniform, culled, runaway, split - and on nothing else: bay A measures its population in leg length, bay B in crown radius, bay C in sphere radius and bay D in distance from the population's own centroid, all four in metres and with no unit conversion between any two of them. Walk the selection axis and three of the four turn out to say the same thing about `culled` - the survivor is untouched, identical to the byte - while the fourth has no `runaway` at all and stands empty at it, pad and plinth and rail still there. The second channel drops the heights and shows only how many of the population is still standing, where the same five-word vocabulary collapses to THREE pictures.
dev_themes: a shared vocabulary that shares nothing else
counted by heads, five words are three
the bay that does not have the word
interactions: read the row left to right at drift - four substrates, four different pictures of no pressure at all
walk to uniform and then to culled and watch bays A, B and C not move: three codebases agreeing that culling does not touch the survivor
walk to runaway and find bay D empty - the fourth vocabulary saying it does not have the word
switch to count and watch drift, uniform and split become one picture in every bay
pressure_yard.capacity: SEE that a shared value list is not a shared meaning. Five words are declared identically by four independently written substrates, and underneath them sit four incommensurable quantities - a limb length, a crown radius, a sphere radius and a displacement from a centroid - plus one substrate that cannot express the fourth word at all. SEE ALSO that a selection statement makes two separable claims, how far apart the survivors stand and how many there are, and that the second one flattens three of the five words into one picture.
pressure_yard.qfep_connection: F is the token: one string out of five, spelled the same in four registry entries and matched character for character by four `match` statements. E is the four irreducible readings - metres of leg, metres of crown, metres of radius, metres from the centroid - which cannot be converted into one another because there is no quantity all four populations share. lambda is how much of the word each substrate is willing to implement: three implement five values, one implements four and says so on the record. The dark spot is the AGREEMENT. Three substrates written by three hands agree exactly about `culled` - the survivor is untouched - and that agreement has never been visible, because no two of these populations have ever stood in the same frame. The row exists to make the agreement checkable, and the same arrangement is what makes the disagreements checkable too; neither was available while each substrate had its own room.
pressure_yard.relationships:
Synthesised out of the four scenes that declare a `selection` axis, reached through six registry names: [[evolved_creatures]] (algorithms/machinelearning/carlsims/evolvedcreatures.gd), [[evolvingflowers]] and its alias [[evolving_flowers]] (algorithms/machinelearning/evolvingflowers/evolvingflowers.gd), [[non_teleological_evolution]], and [[evolutionary_algorithms]] with its alias [[particle_randomness_evolutionary]], which resolve to one scene whose root script extends algorithms/randomness/proceduralrandomness/particlerandomness/extrem_randomness.gd.

SIBLING AND COUNTERPART: [[selection_garden]], promoted the same day out of the same four files. The two are the two halves of one question and neither substitutes for the other. selection_garden holds the SUBSTRATE constant - one founding population, one hash stream, one `_run_regime` called five times - and stands the five regimes side by side, so the thing it can see is what selection did. This yard holds the REGIME constant and stands the four substrates side by side, so the thing it can see is what the word means. selection_garden EXHIBITS `selection` and sweeps `variation` x `evidence`; this yard SWEEPS `selection` and exhibits the substrates. Read together they answer the family's two open questions; read alone, either can be mistaken for the whole.

CONSTRUCTION BORROWED FROM [[tier_terrarium]]: two channels that pin each other, so neither can read the other's number (there: body varied extent at a pinned facet count, grain varied facet count at a pinned height). Here spread varies height at a pinned headcount of six and count varies headcount on a pinned ladder of rungs.

LAW 10 KIN: [[taxonomy_hall]] and [[selection_garden]] are the corpus's other sparse-not-small subjects, and this one is sparser than either.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: THE HEIGHT IS THE CONSTRAINT, NOT THE FOOTPRINT. The plinth is 5.400 x 0.240 m, which is six cells by one, but the rack stands 4.040 m from the underside of the plinth to the top of the datum rail (RAIL_Y 3.860 + RAIL_SIZE.y/2 0.060, less PLINTH_Y - PLINTH_SIZE.y/2 = -0.120). That needs FIVE cells of headroom, and a ceiling at 4 will decapitate the datum rail - which is the reference every bay is read against, so losing it costs the exhibit its whole argument rather than a detail. front 4 because a 5.40 m row read at eye height wants the reader back far enough to hold four bays at once; back 0 because everything the axes draw faces the approach and the rack is 0.24 m deep.

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry - the rack is boxes at named constants, so this AABB is arithmetic and not a Godot measurement pass. x = PLINTH_SIZE.x = 5.400 (the plinth is the widest thing at every variant; the outermost slat reaches only 2.100 + 0.450 = 2.550). y = -0.120 (plinth underside) to 3.920 (rail top) = 4.040; the tallest slat the rack can build tops out at BASE_Y + TRAVEL + SLAT_THICK = 3.690, which is why the rail and not a slat sets the ceiling. z = PLINTH_SIZE.z = 0.240. IDENTICAL AT ALL TEN VARIANTS, which is load bearing - see dna.still_note. Re-measure when a Godot pass is run.

dna.default:
selection=drift, channel=spread.

BOTH ARE THE CODE'S OWN @export DEFAULTS, read off pressure_yard.gd:251 and :262 and not chosen here. There are no shipped placements to preserve (dna.placements is 0, verified: no map_data.json and no JSON under commons/ names this token), so the defaults had only to be the strongest single readings, and they are.

drift is additionally the @export default of THREE of the four source scenes - evolvedcreatures.gd:45, evolvingflowers.gd:63, non_teleological_evolution.gd:71 all read `var selection: String = "drift"` - and it is the un-pressured state every other value is a departure from. Opening anywhere else would open on a claim.

channel=spread because at spread all ten selection pairs differ somewhere, and at count three of the five values are ONE picture. Measured in the Python raster: the count channel's drift, uniform and split tiles are identical to the byte in all four bays, so opening on count would open on a sheet where three fifths of the axis is a single frame shown three times.

DECLARED ORDER IS selection THEN channel, and the arithmetic is in dna.budget. It matters less here than in tier_terrarium because the cross product is 10 against build_dna_gallery's default cap of 16, so at the default NOTHING is trimmed - but it decides what breaks at a lowered cap, and the answer is worse than the source file's comment suggests. See dna.budget.
dna.was: nothing. This token did not exist before this pass, and neither did the arrangement. Measured, not assumed: a sweep of all 108 registry files returns exactly six entries declaring a `selection` axis - evolved_creatures, evolving_flowers, evolvingflowers, non_teleological_evolution in machinelearning.json, and evolutionary_algorithms, particle_randomness_evolutionary in randomness.json. Four of the six declare [drift, uniform, culled, runaway, split]; two declare [drift, uniform, culled, split]. The six resolve to four scene paths. No two of these populations have ever appeared in one frame, so the question of whether the shared word names a shared thing could not be put.
dna.note:
WHAT THE WORD MEANS IN EACH CODEBASE, re-derived from the four source files for this entry rather than transcribed from the artifact's own header. Every line number below was opened and read.

  A  evolved_creatures / evolvedcreatures.gd - LEG LENGTH IN METRES. One scalar, leg_size.y, taking LEG_SIZE_WILD 0.80 (:56), LEG_SIZE_CONVERGED 1.15 (:58), LEG_SIZE_RUNAWAY 2.50 (:60), LEG_SIZE_SPLIT_SHORT 0.45 and LEG_SIZE_SPLIT_LONG 1.60 (:61-62). POPULATION_SIZE 20 (:23), CULLED_SLOTS 4 entries (:98).
  B  evolvingflowers.gd - CROWN RADIUS IN METRES, center_size + petal_length. POPULATION_SIZE 16 (:53), CULLED_PLOTS 3 entries (:75). _optimum_genome 0.30 + 1.00 (:385-391), _runaway_genome 0.40 + 1.50 (:409-415), _split_genome west 0.25 + 0.70 and east 0.35 + 1.30 (:433-455). `drift` is the only value with a DISTRIBUTION rather than authored genomes: _drift_genome draws petal_length uniform on 0.5..1.5 (:362) and center_size uniform on 0.2..0.5 (:365) INDEPENDENTLY, so the crown radius is a trapezoidal sum and its quantiles pile up in the middle.
  C  non_teleological_evolution.gd - SPHERE RADIUS IN METRES. There is no body plan at all. UNIFORM_RADIUS 0.035 (:86), CULLED_RADIUS 0.035 (:92), RUNAWAY_RADIUS 0.05 (:97), SPLIT_SMALL 0.022 and SPLIT_LARGE 0.048 (:106-107), drift drawn uniform on 0.02..0.05 (:289). initial_population 30 (:45), max_population 120 (:46), CULLED_COUNT 6 (:89).
  D  evolutionary_algorithms / extrem_randomness.gd - DISTANCE FROM THE POPULATION'S OWN CENTROID, IN METRES. This substrate has no genome and no trait, so the thing selection acts on IS the coordinate. num_particles 100 (:8), SPLIT_SEPARATION 1.25 (:95).

WHERE THEY AGREE, and it is the sharpest falsifiable thing in the row. Three of the four say the same thing about `culled`, and they were written by three different hands: culling removes members WITHOUT TOUCHING THE SURVIVOR. Bay A returns LEG_SIZE_CONVERGED for both uniform and culled (:322-329); bay B calls _optimum_genome on both branches; bay C's UNIFORM_RADIUS 0.035 IS its CULLED_RADIUS 0.035. So in the spread channel bays A, B and C at uniform and at culled must be IDENTICAL TO THE BYTE. Confirmed in the raster: 0.000% in all three, 16.050% in bay D alone.

WHERE THEY DISAGREE, and none of it is a detail:

  1. `runaway` DOES NOT EXIST in bay D. extrem_randomness.gd:86 declares FOUR strings, ["drift", "uniform", "culled", "split"], verified character for character; _apply_selection (:634-638) returns early on anything else and _winner_count (:501-506) has no runaway branch. The family's runaway means the population standing at its own max_population ceiling, and this substrate has no ceiling because it has no birth - `particles` is appended to at exactly ONE site, inside create_particles (:208), and is never grown, shortened, cleared or erased anywhere in the file. So bay D stands EMPTY at runaway.
  2. ONLY ONE BAY'S runaway IS A HEADCOUNT. Bay C grows 30 -> 120 bodies. Bays A and B keep their 20 and their 16 and grow the BODY instead. So the same word names a population size in one vocabulary and a body size in two others.
  3. `culled` IS THE ONLY VALUE THAT MOVES THE HEADCOUNT in A, B and C - 20->4, 16->3, 30->6 - and it moves NOTHING in D, where nothing is ever born and nothing ever dies. The mirror image of point 1, and the raster shows it as a mirror image: count uniform/culled is 0.000% in bay D alone and non-zero in A, B and C.

THE FINDING THE ROW EXISTS FOR: counted by heads, a five-word vocabulary is THREE words. No substrate changes headcount between drift, uniform and split - 20/20/20, 16/16/16, 30/30/30, 100/100/100 - so those three count-channel tiles are byte identical in all four bays and the critic will name three twins at 0.000%. That is not a design fault and must not be filed as one; read the axis by CO-AXIS CONTEXT, not by its mean (the csg_union_demo precedent, where flush/seam/shared measured 0.00% to the byte at fusion=distinct because there was no join to mark). Measured means: selection reads 3.2886% frame / 21.5958% focus at channel=spread against 1.8099% / 14.7011% at channel=count.

CORRECTIONS TO THE RECORD (LAW 1: the code wins), both re-verified here rather than taken on the artifact's word:

  - machinelearning.json's evolved_creatures entry says "Morphology and behavior co-evolve". FALSE at all five values. _mutate (evolvedcreatures.gd:544-555) touches hip_amplitude, hip_frequency, hip_phase, torso_mass and leg_mass and NOTHING else - never torso_size, never leg_size. The drawn body is a constant per value. Only the masses, which are never drawn, and the gait, which is invisible in a still, evolve at all.
  - evolvingflowers' `_optimum_genome` is not the optimum on its own fitness function. Not load bearing here, because bay B renders crown radius and not fitness, but the row must not be captioned as if `uniform` were the substrate's best answer.
  - BAY D'S NUMBERS ARE THE ONLY ONES THAT ARE NOT LITERALS, and this is the weakest thing in the pass, stated so it cannot be discovered later as a surprise. A, B and C read their spread off named constants. extrem_randomness has no trait and no literal spread except SPLIT_SEPARATION 1.25; the artifact's D_DRIFT_MAX 1.600, D_UNIFORM_MAX 0.950 and D_CULLED_MAX 0.090 are integrated from per-frame velocity constants (0.9 damping, 0.5 follow, 2.0 beeline, none scaled by delta) over the harness's 1.1 s settle, so in the SOURCE they move with frame rate and are facts about the capture as much as about the artifact. They are baked here as declared constants because LAWS 4 and 5 forbid simulating them. Read the other way this is the row's sharpest answer: in one of the four currencies the word does not name a quantity that exists at t = 0.
dna.kin:
`selection` IS TAKEN, not refused, and taken character for character (LAW 13): ["drift", "uniform", "culled", "runaway", "split"], the list all four five-value declarers carry, in that order. Verified against evolvedcreatures.gd:45, evolvingflowers.gd:63 and non_teleological_evolution.gd:71, all three of which spell it as an @export_enum in exactly this sequence.

THE FOURTH DECLARES FOUR OF THE FIVE AND ITS REFUSAL IS DRAWN RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER. extrem_randomness.gd:86 is ["drift", "uniform", "culled", "split"] - a SUBSET, not a disagreement, and a refusal its own note put on the record before this pass. The rejected alternative was to reproduce the RUNTIME behaviour, where an unknown value silently leaves whatever was last built in force. That would publish a silent fallback as an answer, which is the science_screen failure exactly: a typo ran every stage green and the verdict turned out to be a fact about the registry. The bay stands empty instead, with its pad and the plinth and the rail still there, so it reads as an unpopulated bay and not as a short row.

WHERE THIS ARTIFACT IS WEAKER THAN ITS SIBLING, on the record. [[selection_garden]] reads the family list at RUN TIME out of the owner file (it preloads non_teleological_evolution.gd and compares against SELECTION_SRC.SELECTIONS), so a drift in the family's own vocabulary would break its build. This yard retypes the five strings as its own const SELECTIONS and then checks them against its OWN @export hint_string in both directions, membership and order (_check_hint, :678-700). That check is real - it is the defence science_screen did not have, and it catches the case where the const and the export disagree - but BOTH SIDES OF IT ARE INTERNAL. If evolvedcreatures.gd renamed a value tomorrow, this artifact would keep declaring the old one and every gate would stay green. The cheap repair is a preload of the owner file and a third comparison; it is not made here because extrem_randomness.gd, the file that owns the four-value subset, carries a class_name-free but heavyweight body, and the hand check was done instead: all four lists were opened and compared for this entry, today.

`channel` IS REUSED, NOT MINTED. It is a two-member word across two files ([[operational_eye]], [[tier_terrarium]]), measured rather than assumed, and growing a small existing word was preferred to a sixth name for "which output of the same instrument is on show". The side effect is the useful one: this row and tier_terrarium are now directly comparable, and they are built on the same construction - two channels that pin each other so neither can read the other's number.

ITS TWO VALUES ARE NOT INVENTED EITHER. spread and count are the two separable claims a selection statement makes about a population - how far apart its members stand in their own currency, and how many of them are still standing - and they map onto two disjoint sets of source constants: the radius/length/genome constants on one side, POPULATION_SIZE / CULLED_SLOTS / CULLED_PLOTS / CULLED_COUNT / max_population / num_particles on the other. Nothing in the count channel reads a metre and nothing in the spread channel reads a headcount.
dna.declines:
`generations` REFUSED. Every source runs a generation loop and it is the obvious third axis. It is a CLOCK: a gen-6 and a gen-40 population under one taste land on the same picture, and the family has already refused the same knob twice - genetic_tree_sculptor's `generations` and evolvingflowers' `generation_time`, a 3-to-30-second dial. LAW 4: one still per variant cannot see a rate.

`mobility`, `energy_decay` AND EVERY OTHER RATE REFUSED, same reason, and this is the info_board fault the corpus keeps paying for - five duration exports swept into six identical tiles, a finished-looking experiment that answered nothing.

THE FAMILY'S PER-VALUE HUES REFUSED. non_teleological_evolution carries UNIFORM_HUE, CULLED_HUE, RUNAWAY_HUE and two SPLIT hues, and lipping each bay in its value's colour was the obvious tribute. It is refused because a colour keyed to the value's NAME would hand the eye a difference the substrates did not produce; and `drift` has no hue constant to borrow anyway. ONE material for every slat in every bay (pressure_yard.gd:582-589), so any inequality in measured response is about the vocabulary and not about the drawing.

SURVIVORSHIP PATTERN FORECLOSED, and it is the real cost of the six-order-statistic reading. Bay A's culled keeps the four CORNER slots [0,4,15,19]; bay B keeps plots [0,6,11], no two sharing a row or column; bay C RE-PACKS six survivors into a fresh 3x2 block rather than keeping a subset of the thirty. Which members survive is gone, and so is the third question the family answers - how many distinct KINDS are left - which is the only readout that would separate drift from uniform where headcount cannot.

THE REAL HEADCOUNTS NOT DRAWN, deliberately. Six marks needing 10 px of body and 10 px of gap want 120 px against a travel of 103.93 px, which is why the rack holds SIX slats and not eight, and why each population is six order statistics rather than its 20 / 16 / 30 / 100 individuals. Drawing the real headcount would put every individual at 3-5 px - which is exactly the size at which the source artifacts' own marks already measure as nothing.

NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED NEEDED, and it is checkable rather than claimed. Every source substrate is live at at least one value and every one of them destroys its own still: evolved_creatures spawns RigidBody3D with 1.2 m of air under the feet; evolvingflowers spins each head at 0.2 rad/s and tweens from scale 0.01 with TRANS_ELASTIC overshoot; non_teleological runs _process at drift; evolutionary_algorithms chases a Lissajous target driven by Time.get_ticks_msec. pressure_yard.gd contains no randf, no randi, no randomize, no RandomNumberGenerator, no _process, no timer, no tween, no signal, no physics and no clock read - grep returns seven hits for those tokens and ALL SEVEN are inside comments (:227-230, :289, :291, :302). _ready is ungated and builds the finished row from the two exports in one frame.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS ALL TEN VARIANTS, computed by enumerating every box _build would create at all 5 x 2 combinations. The plinth, the datum rail and the four pads are present in every variant and set all three extents on their own: x = 5.400 (the outermost slat reaches only 2.550), y = -0.120 to 3.920 = 4.040 (the tallest slat the rack can build tops out at 3.690, so the rail sets the ceiling), z = 0.240. Union 5.400 x 4.040 x 0.240, diagonal 6.748274, radius 3.374137.

THE RIG: dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing = 3.374137 / 0.3057307 * 1.9 * 0.46 = 9.645730 m, so the visible frame is 2 * PAD * radius * framing = 5.897991 m and a 760 px still is 128.858 px per metre.

WHY 0.46. At framing 1.0 the rig fits by bounding SPHERE and the row would be 35.4% of frame width - the thin-subject case LAW 9 exists for. At 0.46 the projected box is 5.400 * 0.813869 + 0.240 * 0.581037 = 4.534341 m wide (76.88% of frame) and 5.400 * 0.149373 + 4.040 * 0.966362 + 0.240 * 0.209205 = 4.760926 m tall (80.72% of frame). Below about 0.3714 the box's own height exceeds the frame; 0.46 keeps 9.6% of margin above and below and 11.6% either side, which is the room the showcase key light's specular fringe needs and the replica does not model.

0.46 IS ALSO NOT FREE TO CHANGE, and that is the stronger reason. Every pixel figure the source file gauged its geometry against was computed at it - see dna.still_note - so lowering it re-scales the published tile and invalidates the daylight and bay-crop numbers a reader is told to check the 80-cell table with.

THE GAUGE THE VERDICT IS COMPUTED ON IS NOT THE FRAME, and this is the part that is easy to get wrong by a factor of 1.3. artifact_dna_critic crops each pair to the union of the two subject bboxes (:320-334) and only THEN resizes to 160 x 160 (:93), so framing cancels out of the mark gauge entirely: 160 / 4.534341 = 35.286 px per screen-x metre and 160 / 4.760926 = 33.607 px per screen-y metre. Computing from the visible frame width instead gives 27.176 px/m, a 1.30x understatement of every mark.

EVERY MARK GAUGED AGAINST THAT BEFORE IT WAS DRAWN (LAW 9), and a slab's LAW-9 size is its LOCAL SCREEN THICKNESS, not its bbox extent. A slat's screen-y bbox spans 14.8 px, but 4.5 px of that is the rake of its own 0.900 m length across the pitched view; what a vertical move actually sweeps at fixed screen-x is 2 * (hy * 0.966362 + hz * 0.209205) = 10.54 px at k=0 and 10.08 px at k=5, both over the 10 px floor. Sizing off the bbox would have shipped a 6.3 px mark reported as 15. The bay pitch of 1.400 m is 106.4 px in the published tile.
dna.still_note:
READ THE Z-STACK BEFORE BELIEVING ANY NUMBER OFF THIS SHEET.

NOTHING OPAQUE SITS IN FRONT OF A MARK (LAW 8). The whole scene is boxes at z = 0 with three depths only: plinth -0.120..+0.120, pads -0.060..+0.060, rail -0.060..+0.060, slats -0.080..+0.080 shrinking to -0.070..+0.070. The plinth sits BELOW every slat (its top is y = 0.000, the lowest slat centre is 0.200 + 0.145) and the rail ABOVE every slat (its underside is 3.800 against a maximum slat top of 3.690, a 0.110 m clearance the artifact asserts at run time, :765-768). The only enclosing bodies in the scene are slats, and a slat encloses only slats carrying the IDENTICAL number - the concentric nesting in all three axes (0.900-0.012k, 0.290-0.002k, 0.160-0.004k) exists so that a monomorphic population renders as slat 0 alone rather than as six coplanar faces of z-fighting speckle, which would be a non-deterministic still. There is no bezel, no case and no glass. operations_gallery's bezel was one 24 mm slab enclosing the panel face and every mark its axis drew, and it swept at 0.09% with the subject at 70.3% of frame.

ADJACENT BAYS DO NOT STAND IN EACH OTHER'S LIGHT (LAW 7), and the pitch was set by that arithmetic. At yaw 0.62 a box of half-extents (hx, hy, hz) has a screen-x half-extent of hx * cos(0.62) + hz * sin(0.62). The widest tenant over all ten variants is slat 0 (hx 0.450, hz 0.080): 0.450 * 0.813869 + 0.080 * 0.581037 = 0.412724 m. Bay centres are PITCH * cos(0.62) = 1.139417 m apart. DAYLIGHT = 1.139417 - 2 * 0.412724 = 0.313969 m, which is 11.08 px on the critic's crop and 40.5 px in the published tile. Minimum legal pitch is 1.014 m; 1.400 is 1.38x that, so this is a margin and not a hairline. The six slats are coaxial in x and z, so there is no intra-bay occlusion term.

THE SUBJECT IS AIRY, NOT SMALL (LAW 10), and this is a sparser case than either taxonomy_hall or tier_terrarium. Rasterised subject share swings 8.43% (spread, runaway) to 21.43% (spread, drift), because a monomorphic or emptied bay renders one slat where a dispersed bay renders six; the critic takes the MAX over tiles, so it will report ~21.4% and there is no NO RENDER risk. The union box is 76.88% of frame WIDTH and 80.72% of frame HEIGHT - 62.06% of frame AREA - so at its fullest the box is only 34.5% inked and at its emptiest 13.6%. Most of a bay's bounding volume is the empty travel above and below its slats, BY CONSTRUCTION. The swing in subject share is the axis working. Do not tighten dna.framing on it.

THE FURNITURE IS IDENTICAL IN ALL TEN VARIANTS AND THAT IS LOAD BEARING. capture_config_sweep.gd:435 recomputes the radius from each variant's own box when no union pre-pass is available and :442-444 places the camera from it. Because bay D empties at runaway and every rack changes height with the value, a row WITHOUT the plinth and rail would move the camera between tiles and the critic would diff two differently-scaled images - measuring the harness, not the axis. The plinth and rail are what make the ten crops congruent and the ten subject bboxes identical. Being byte-identical they also contribute exactly 0 px to all 25 pair-diffs; the furniture costs the measurement nothing and only has to be legible to a person, which at 4.8-5.6 px it is.

THREE TWINS WILL BE REPORTED AND THEY ARE THE DESIGN. count/drift, count/uniform and count/split are one image, so the critic's twin check (TWIN_FOCUS 0.060) will name all three pairs at 0.000%. That is the null test, not a fault - see dna.predicted_relationship.
dna.predicted_relationship:
FIVE CLAIMS, ALL FALSIFIABLE, ALL STATED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE. Claims 1-4 are asserted at run time by _check_relationship (:721-768) and push_error on failure; claim 5 is measured off the tiles.

(1) THE PINNING, BOTH DIRECTIONS. In `spread` every populated bay carries EXACTLY SIX slats at every value, so headcount carries literally zero signal; in `count` every occupied slat stands on a FIXED RUNG at an identical world height in every bay at every value, so height carries zero. Neither channel can read the other's number. FALSIFYING THRESHOLD: if any count-channel pair's signal turns out to depend on a bay's spread ladder, or any spread-channel pair on a headcount, the channels are entangled and neither number means what this entry says. First thing to check: whether _build_bay is reading _spread_ladder in the count branch.

(2) THE NULL TEST, AND IT IS A TWO-SIDED GATE. No substrate changes headcount between drift, uniform and split (20/20/20, 16/16/16, 30/30/30, 100/100/100), so those three count-channel tiles must be byte identical in all four bays: three pairs at EXACTLY 0.000% frame and 0.000% focus. Verified per-bay in the raster - count drift/uniform is 0.000% in A, B, C and D separately. ANY NONZERO READING THERE IS NOT A FINDING ABOUT SELECTION. It is proof that the rig is not deterministic, and it invalidates every other number in the pass.

(3) THE EQUALITY, which is the sharpest thing the row asserts and cannot come out right by luck. Three independently written codebases all say culling does not touch the survivor, so in the SPREAD channel bays A, B and C must be identical between uniform and culled, and bay D must NOT be. Raster, per bay crop: A 0.000%, B 0.000%, C 0.000%, D 16.050% frame / 66.311% focus. The whole of the closest live pair's signal comes from one bay. THE MIRROR IMAGE IS ALSO PREDICTED: in the COUNT channel the same pair must be non-zero in A, B and C and zero in D, because D is where nothing is born and nothing dies - raster: A 8.603%, B 12.005%, C 3.718%, D 0.000%. FALSIFYING THRESHOLD: any of those four zeros measuring focus > 2.0% on its bay crop, or any of those four non-zeros measuring < 2.0%.

dna.budget:
5 x 2 = 10 variants against build_dna_gallery's default cap of 16 (tools/build_dna_gallery.py:136), so AT THE DEFAULT NOTHING IS TRIMMED and the coverage record is complete. The dot_aligner fault - a four-value axis rendered at two and judged as four - cannot occur at this size.

DO NOT RUN THIS SWEEP BELOW --max=10, and the reason is worse than the source file's comment suggests. build_dna_gallery trims values from the END of the LATER axis until the running cross product fits (sweep(), :78-96). With selection declared first, at cap 9: selection keeps all five (5 <= 9), then channel is trimmed from 2 to 1, which is fewer than 2, so `channel` IS DROPPED ENTIRELY - not shortened. The sheet becomes a single-axis sweep with the channel silently pinned at its default, and the manifest lists what rendered, so a dropped axis looks exactly like an undeclared one. The source file's note says count 'would lose values before split did'; a two-value axis losing a value means being dropped whole, and that is the accurate statement. With channel declared first, cap 9 would instead render 2 x 4 = 8 and drop `split` - which is the row's sharpest finding, the value that is bimodal in three currencies and unimodal in the fourth. Both sacrifices are bad. The ruling is the cap, not the order.

The synthesis's stated argument is that each substrate renders a selection statement in a different currency - limb length in metres, petal count, sphere radius and hue, position in a fitness landscape. Normalising all four onto one order-statistic rack is what makes them comparable, and it is also what removes the thing being claimed: every bay draws the identical white slat and a viewer cannot see which currency any bay is in. The difference survives in this registry and not in the still. Whether that trade is right is a curatorial call and is NOT settled here. ALSO VISIBLE IN THE SHEET, and only in the sheet: at channel=spread several bays FUSE into a single slab where their six order statistics coincide. At uniform that is honest and is the point - a converged population is one block. At drift it is honest for a different and sharper reason found by the source readers: evolved_creatures' drift is not a spread at all but a regular lattice of 20 geometrically identical bipeds, because randomize() never touches torso_size or leg_size. The word promises a spread and the code delivers a lattice.
